title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask friends if they're free, suggest what to do, fix a time and place, tell them you're on your way or stuck in traffic, and cancel without offending anyone.
intro:
Welcome to Part 2! From here on the course is about the Nepali you'll use with friends, in shops and on the street. We start with the thing friends do most: making plans — and then changing them.

You'll learn the friendly **तिमी** commands (आऊ, पर्ख, ढिलो नगर है!), the 'shall we?' question **कहाँ भेट्ने?**, the coaxing **जाऔँ न!**, and how to say 'I'm about to leave' (**निस्कन लागेको**), 'I'm on my way' (**बाटोमा छु**) and 'I'll be right there' (**आइहाल्छु**). Expect plenty of English words — **फ्री**, **बिजी**, **प्लान**, **क्यान्सिल** — because that's how young Kathmandu really talks.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…? with friends
grammar.body:
In unit 18 you met **-औँ** 'let's' (जाऔँ) and **-ऊँ** 'shall I?' (म आऊँ?). Among friends, plans are made with a few more forms:

**-ने?** — the bare -ने form as a question is the most common way to ask 'shall we…?': **कहाँ भेट्ने?** 'where shall we meet?', **के खाने?** 'what shall we eat?', **जाने?** 'shall we go?', **जाने कि नजाने?** 'are we going or not?'. It has no person ending, so it works for anyone.

**-औँ न** — 'come on, let's…' (persuading): **जाऔँ न!**, **अर्को दिन गरौँ न** 'let's do it another day'. **-औँ त** — 'let's (just) see / try': **हेरौँ त**.

**-औँला** — 'we'll (probably)…' (unit 17): **भेटौँला** 'we'll meet (some time)' — friendly but vague! For a fixed plan use the present: भोलि सात बजे **भेट्छौँ** 'we're meeting at seven tomorrow'.

Replies: **हुन्छ** 'OK', **जाऔँ जाऔँ!** / **जाने जाने!** 'yes, let's!', **चल्छ** 'that works', **हिँड** 'let's go', **हेरौँ** 'let's see' — which often means 'probably not'.

examples.en: Where shall we go this evening?
Are we going to see the film or not?
Come on, let's go on a picnic on Saturday!

examples.native: हेरौँ, फ्री भएँ भने फोन गर्छु।
examples.roman: herauṃ, phri bhaeṃ bhane phon garchhu.
examples.en: Let's see — if I'm free I'll call.

grammar.title: Telling a friend what to do: the तिमी command
grammar.body:
With **तिमी** (friends, younger people) commands are short:

**Consonant stems** use the bare stem, said with a final *a*: गर *gara* 'do', बस *basa* 'sit', हेर *hera* 'look', सुन *suna* 'listen', पर्ख *parkha* 'wait', कुर *kura* 'wait for'.
**Vowel stems** end in **-ऊ**: खाऊ *khāu*, जाऊ *jāu*, आऊ *āu*, बताऊ *batāu*; दिनु → **देऊ** *deu*, लिनु → **लेऊ** *leu*.
**Negative**: put **न-** in front: **नगर** 'don't (do)', **नजाऊ**, **नकुर** 'don't wait'.

On its own a command can sound bossy, so friends add a particle: **न** 'come on, please' (आऊ **न**), **त** 'just, then' (हेर **त**), **है** 'OK?' (ढिलो नगर **है**). For something to do later there is a special form in **-नू**: भोलि बेलैमा **आउनू** है 'be on time tomorrow, OK?'.

Close friends — especially young men — often drop to **तँ**, whose command has no ending at all: **गर्**, **बस्**, **हिँड्**, जा, खा, and the irregular **आइज** 'come'. Recognise it, but stick to तिमी until your friends use तँ with you. With anyone older use **-नुहोस्**, which in speech is usually shortened to **-नुस्**: बस्नुस्, आउनुस्.

examples.native: छिटो आऊ न, सबै कुर्दै छन्।
examples.roman: chhiṭo āu na, sabai kurdai chhan.

examples.en: Make sure you're on time tomorrow.
(तँ, to a close mate) Come on, we're late!

grammar.title: About to, on the way, nearly there
grammar.body:
Plans live or die in the last half hour: 'I'm leaving now', 'I'm on the way', 'nearly there'. Nepali has a set of forms for this:

**-न लाग्नु** 'to be about to': म निस्कन **लागेको** or म निस्कन **लागेँ** 'I'm just about to leave'; पानी पर्न **लाग्यो** 'it's about to rain'; बस छुट्न **लाग्यो** 'the bus is about to go'. In the past: म सुत्न **लागेको थिएँ** 'I was about to go to bed'.

**-दै छु** (unit 10) for 'on my way': म **आउँदै छु** 'I'm coming', हामी **जाँदै छौँ** 'we're on our way'. Just as common: **म बाटोमा छु** 'I'm on the way'.

**-इहाल्नु** 'right away, at once': म **आइहाल्छु** 'I'll be right there', **खाइहाल** 'go ahead and eat (don't wait)'. And **-इसक्नु** 'already' (unit 17): म **पुगिसकेँ** 'I'm already here'; the question is **कहाँ पुग्यौ?** 'where have you got to?'.

Know that Nepali time is elastic: **आउँदै छु** can mean 'I'm putting my shoes on', and **पाँच मिनेट** can easily be twenty.

examples.native: म निस्कन लागेको, पाँच मिनेट कुर।
examples.roman: ma niskana lāgeko, pāṃch mineṭ kura.
examples.en: I'm about to leave — give me five minutes.
I'm on my way, nearly there.
You guys go ahead and eat, I'll be right there.
It's about to rain, walk faster.

dialogue.title: Momos at seven
dialogue.setting: Prakash rings Rojina on a Friday afternoon to round up friends for momos in Jhamsikhel. Then, at seven, she is there and he isn't.

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.native: हेलो रोजिना, के छ? आज बेलुका फ्री छौ?
lines.roman: helo Rojinā, ke chha? āja belukā phri chhau?
lines.en: Hi Rojina, what's up? Are you free this evening?

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.native: अमित र सुमन पनि आउँदै छन्। साढे छ बजे झम्सिखेलमा मःम खान जाने?
lines.roman: Amit ra Suman pani āuṃdai chhan. sāḍhe chha baje Jhamsikhelmā momo khāna jāne?
lines.en: Amit and Suman are coming too. Shall we go for momos in Jhamsikhel at half six?

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: जाने जाने! तर साढे छ बजे त मलाई भ्याइँदैन। सात बजे चल्छ?
lines.roman: jāne jāne! tara sāḍhe chha baje ta malāi bhyāiṃdaina. sāt baje chalchha?
lines.en: Yes, let's! But I can't make half six. Does seven work?

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.native: हुन्छ, सात बजे। म बाइकमा तिमीलाई लिन आउँछु नि।
lines.roman: hunchha, sāt baje. ma bāikmā timilāi lina āuṃchhu ni.
lines.en: OK, seven. I'll come and get you on the bike.

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: पर्दैन, म आफैँ आउँछु। ढिलो नगर है!
lines.roman: pardaina, ma āphaiṃ āuṃchhu. ḍhilo nagara hai!
lines.en: No need, I'll come by myself. Don't be late!

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: ए प्रकाश, कहाँ पुग्यौ? म त पुगिसकेँ।
lines.roman: e Prakās, kahāṃ pugyau? ma ta pugisakeṃ.
lines.en: Hey Prakash, where've you got to? I'm already here.

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.native: सरी सरी! म बाटोमा छु, कोटेश्वरमा जाममा परेँ।
lines.roman: sari sari! ma bāṭomā chhu, Koṭeswarmā jāmmā pareṃ.
lines.en: Sorry, sorry! I'm on my way — I got stuck in traffic at Koteshwor.

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: फेरि जाम? तिमी सधैँ ढिलो गर्छौ यार!
lines.roman: pheri jām? timi sadhaiṃ ḍhilo garchhau yār!
lines.en: Traffic again? You're always late, man!

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.native: दस मिनेटमा आइपुग्छु, पक्का! मलाई नकुर, खान सुरु गर।
lines.roman: das mineṭmā āipugchhu, pakkā! malāi nakura, khāna suru gara.
lines.en: I'll be there in ten minutes, promise! Don't wait for me, start eating.

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: हुन्छ, तर आजको बिल तिमीले तिर्ने!
lines.roman: hunchha, tara ājako bil timile tirne!

lines.speaker: Prakash
lines.en: Alright, I'll pay, I'll pay. I'm basically there!

culture: Plans among Nepali friends are loose and made late: 'shall we?' at five for seven o'clock is normal, and a group chat decides the rest. Saturday is the one full day off for most people, so Friday evening and Saturday are when everyone meets up. Being late is so common that **जाममा परेँ** is a running joke — Kathmandu's traffic is real, but so is 'Nepali time'. When saying no, people rarely refuse flatly: **हेरौँ** 'let's see', **कोसिस गर्छु** 'I'll try' and **अर्को दिन** 'another day' are the usual soft no's, and friends understand them that way. Whoever suggests the outing often ends up paying (or is teased into it), though splitting is increasingly normal among students. In winter (Poush–Magh) the big group outing is the **पिकनिक**: a hired bus, a riverside spot, a borrowed pot and a goat curry. With friends of your age use **तिमी** from the start; save **तपाईं** for older people and anyone you've just met in a formal setting.

tip.title: English words, Nepali verbs
tip.body:
- Plans are full of English: **फ्री**, **बिजी**, **प्लान**, **बोर** — with Nepali verbs after them: फ्री **छौ**?, बोर **भयो**.
- With a friend use **तिमी** forms: फ्री **छौ**? To someone older: फ्री **हुनुहुन्छ**?
- **फुर्सद** 'free time' takes **मलाई**: मलाई फुर्सद छैन.

sentences.en: Are you free tomorrow evening?

sentences.native: आज त म धेरै बिजी छु।
sentences.roman: āja ta ma dherai biji chhu.
sentences.en: I'm really busy today.

sentences.en: I've no time today — is tomorrow OK?
What's the plan for Saturday?
I'm bored of sitting at home.
I'm not in the mood to go out today.
I haven't got any plans — why?
Are you free this evening? (to an older man)

tip.title: Shall we…? Let's…!
tip.body:
- **-ने?** = 'shall we…?': कहाँ **भेट्ने**? के **खाने**? फुटसल खेल्न **जाने**?
- **-औँ न** = 'come on, let's…!': जा**औँ न**!
- **-औँ?** = 'shall we?': यहाँ बस**ौँ**?
- Replies: **हुन्छ**, **जाने जाने!**, **चल्छ**, or the soft no **हेरौँ** 'let's see'.
tip.pattern: कहाँ / के / कति बजे + verb-ने?  ·  verb-औँ न!

sentences.en: Shall we go and play futsal this evening?

sentences.native: हलमा नयाँ फिल्म आएको छ, हेर्न जाने?
sentences.roman: halmā nayāṃ philm āeko chha, herna jāne?
sentences.en: There's a new film on — shall we go and see it?

sentences.native: शनिबार सबै सँगै पिकनिक जाऔँ न!
sentences.roman: sanibār sabai saṃgai pikanik jāauṃ na!
sentences.en: Come on, let's all go on a picnic together on Saturday!
Let's sit in a café somewhere and chat.
What shall we eat, rice or momo?
Shall we meet at the café or at the cinema?
Let's go for a walk together tomorrow morning.
Are we going somewhere today or not?
Let's see, I'll let you know later.

sentences.native: म आज कतै जाँदिनँ, घरमै बस्छु।
sentences.roman: ma āja katai jāṃdinaṃ, gharmai baschhu.
sentences.en: I'm not going anywhere today, I'm staying in.

tip.title: The तिमी command
tip.body:
- Consonant stems: bare stem, said with *a*: **कुर** *kura* 'wait', **बस** *basa* 'sit'.
- Vowel stems: **-ऊ**: आ**ऊ**, जा**ऊ**; दिनु → **देऊ**.
- Don't: **न-** in front: **न**कुर, **न**गर.
- Soften with **न**, **त**, **है**. For later: **-नू** (आउनू है).
- Close mates may use तँ: **हिँड्**, **बस्**.

sentences.en: Wait at the gate, I'm coming.
Come on time, OK!
Hop on my bike, I'll take you.
Tell everyone for me, will you?

sentences.native: ढिलो नगर, सात बजे भेटघाट छ।
sentences.roman: ḍhilo nagara, sāt baje bheṭghāṭ chha.
sentences.en: Don't be late — we're meeting at seven.

sentences.native: मलाई गेटमा नकुर, सिधै भित्र जाऊ।
sentences.roman: malāi geṭmā nakura, sidhai bhitra jāu.
sentences.en: Don't wait for me at the gate, go straight in.
Do be on time tomorrow, OK?

sentences.native: म छ बजे तिमीलाई लिन आउँछु, तयार बस।
sentences.roman: ma chha baje timilāi lina āuṃchhu, tayār basa.
sentences.en: I'll pick you up at six — be ready.

sentences.native: हाम्रो भेटघाट धेरै दिनदेखि भएको छैन।
sentences.roman: hāmro bheṭghāṭ dherai dindekhi bhaeko chhaina.
sentences.en: We haven't met up for ages.
(तँ, to a close mate) Move it, we're late!

tip.title: About to, on the way, right there
tip.body:
- **-न लाग्नु** = 'about to': म निस्क**न लागेँ**, बस छुट्**न लाग्यो**.
- **-दै छु** = 'I'm …ing': म आउ**ँदै छु**. Or simply **बाटोमा छु**.
- **-इहाल्नु** = 'right away': म आ**इहाल्छु** 'I'll be right there'.
- **-इसक्नु** = 'already': म पुग**िसकेँ**.

sentences.en: I'm just about to leave.
The bus is about to go — hurry!
We're on the way, nearly there.

sentences.native: तिमी कहाँ छौ? म त पुगिसकेँ।
sentences.roman: timi kahāṃ chhau? ma ta pugisakeṃ.
sentences.en: Where are you? I'm already here.
I'm coming, hang on a sec.
Sorry, there's a big jam on the way.
He still hasn't got here.
You guys start, I'll be right there.
What time shall we leave?

tip.title: Cancelling without offending
tip.body:
- Give a reason and a quick **सरी यार**: आज त भ्याइँदैन यार.
- Offer another time: **अर्को दिन गरौँ न**, **भोलि सारौँ?** 'shall we move it to tomorrow?'
- **हेरौँ** 'let's see' and **कोसिस गर्छु** 'I'll try' are the polite no — and Nepalis hear them that way.

sentences.en: Sorry mate, I can't make it today.

sentences.native: काम सकेर भ्यायौ भने आऊ न।
sentences.roman: kām sakera bhyāyau bhane āu na.
sentences.en: If you manage to finish work in time, do come.

Shall we move tomorrow's picnic to next week?

sentences.native: आज भ्याइनँ, सरी। भोलि पक्का आउँछु।
sentences.roman: āja bhyāinaṃ, sari. bholi pakkā āuṃchhu.
sentences.en: I couldn't make it today, sorry. Tomorrow for sure.
Let's see — if I can make it, I'll come.

sentences.native: ठीक छ, केही छैन, अर्को पटक भेटौँला।
sentences.roman: ṭhik chha, kehi chhaina, arko paṭak bheṭauṃlā.
sentences.en: That's fine, no worries — we'll meet next time.
